va_6_jaybird_gorge.blurb: Jaybird Gorge is a boulder-heavy pocket of Southwest Virginia, set inside Guest River Gorge and divided into two halves, Lightside and Darkside, that sit on opposite sides of the gorge. Nearly everything here is bouldering, with a small number of sport routes and almost no trad. Problems run from very easy to very hard, but the middle grades, roughly V2 to V5, hold the biggest share, and there is a real tail of V7 and harder. Darkside faces mostly north and stays shady, so it takes far longer to dry after rain or snow, and its boulders are joined by many short crags. Lightside gathers boulders and blocks in its lower zone and receives more sun.

wi_governor_dodge_state_park.blurb: Governor Dodge State Park lies in southern Wisconsin near Dodgeville, where scattered sandstone boulders are the main draw. Bouldering dominates by a wide margin, with the largest clusters in the Group Camps, Cox Hollow and Twin Valley sections, while a few bolted sport lines, some top-rope walls and a handful of winter ice routes fill out the rest. Problems are mostly easy to moderate, about V0 to V5, with a thinner tail of harder ones up to roughly V8. The sandstone is soft: some of it is solid, but much is fragile or crumbly, holds can break, and wet rock is best left alone. Treat it as a gentle, low-key area rather than a hard-charging one.

ak_hatcher_pass.blurb: Hatcher Pass sits in the Talkeetna Range of South Central Alaska, about an hour north of Anchorage, and most of its roped climbing is concentrated in Archangel Valley. The mix is broad: trad is the largest share, followed by bouldering, alpine routes and sport. Roped grades cluster from the 5.7s up through 5.11, with a few harder lines, and the bouldering stretches from easy problems to double-digit V grades. The rock is blocky granite with plenty of moss, and steady rain in spring and fall keeps shaded faces damp. Beyond Archangel, Reed Lakes, Independence Mine and the Glacier Creek drainage add more rock. The area is still being developed and is fast gaining a name as a bouldering destination.

mt_south_central_region.blurb: South Central Montana stretches from Billings toward the Beartooth Mountains and Cooke City, with Red Lodge and Natural Bridge as other hubs. Sport climbing dominates, backed by plenty of trad and top-rope, a little bouldering, and some ice and alpine terrain in the Beartooths. Grades concentrate between 5.10 and 5.12, with a fair number of easier lines and a handful at 5.13 and 5.14. Around Billings the crags are sandstone rimrock cliffs that ring the city and sit close to town; by midday the sun bakes the south-facing walls, so an early start helps in warm weather. The Beartooth side is a different world, remote and leaning toward alpine and ice objectives.

wy_wild_iris.blurb: Wild Iris is a sport-climbing destination on Limestone Mountain southwest of Lander, Wyoming, at high elevation of roughly 9,000 feet. Almost everything is bolted, with a heavy concentration between 5.10 and 5.12 and a lighter spread of easier and harder lines above and below. The rock is pocketed and technical. OK Corral and The Main Wall are the largest sectors, with Aspen Glade, Lower Remuda and The Erratic next. Aspens shade some belay spots, though many climbs face south and can run hot. The season opens once snow melts in early summer and lasts into late fall, and sunny cool days can make it a good fallback when other crags are too warm. Weather can change fast at this height.

mi_550_bouldering.blurb: 550 Bouldering is a forested stretch of boulders north of Marquette in Michigan's Upper Peninsula, strung along the only highway that heads north out of town. Nearly all of it is bouldering. Most problems fall between VB and V3, with a steady tail up to V8 and a few harder. The big clusters are Wetmore Landing, Harlow Lake Pathway and Wetmore Pond Trailhead, and the terrain varies: steep, burly boulders around Lily Pond, slabs at Wetmore Pond, and open boulders with wide views at the Motherlode. The lower spots near wetlands get very buggy from mid-spring through summer, so early spring, fall and winter are the better times to go.
